chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar who said:
The boundary of the Mash'ar al-Haram is from al-Ma'zimayn to al-Hiyad and to Wadi Muhassir, and it is called al-Muzdalifah because they approached it from 'Arafat.

key_terms.اَلْحِيَاضِ: Al-Hiyad, a location marking the end of the Mash'ar boundary.
key_terms.اَلْمَأْزِمَيْنِ: Al-Ma'zimayn, a specific location marking the starting point of the Mash'ar boundary.
key_terms.اَلْمَشْعَرِ اَلْحَرَامِ: The Sacred Station (Mash'ar al-Haram), a key site in Hajj rituals located between 'Arafat and Mina.
key_terms.اَلْمُزْدَلِفَةَ: Al-Muzdalifah, the place where pilgrims gather after leaving 'Arafat.
key_terms.وَادِي مُحَسِّرٍ: Wadi Muhassir, a valley near Muzdalifah.

ai.seo_question: What are the specific boundaries of Mash'ar al-Haram and why is it called Muzdalifah?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the precise geographical limits of Mash'ar al-Haram, a key rite where pilgrims perform the Qasr and Duhur prayers. The etymological note linking 'Muzdalifah' to the act of approaching (*izdalaf*) from Arafat underscores the ritual continuity of the Hajj journey, a concept deeply rooted in Shia fiqh regarding the validity of the stay at Muzdalifah.
